key_insight: Fovea-centered spatial normalization can reduce geometric domain shifts and make OCT retinal layer segmentation more consistent across datasets.
clinical_relevance: More robust segmentation could support more reliable retinal biomarker extraction for neurodegenerative research and other clinical analyses.
method: Align OCT volumes to a common anatomical reference centered on the fovea.
Compare multiple state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation models.
Evaluate with B-scan overlap metrics, A-scan topology metrics, and en-face thickness-based measures.
evidence_signal: The study reports a comprehensive multi-level evaluation, including ground-truth-based metrics and proposed no-ground-truth topology violation and thickness consistency measures.
watch_item: Spatial normalization may improve consistency, but its benefit can depend on accurate fovea localization and may not fully overcome differences in scanners, protocols, or pathology.
paper_title: Spatial Normalization for Cross-Domain Retinal Layer Segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography
